subject.title: feat(slack): allow configurable App Home views

question: Should Slack App Home customization become a permanent public config surface, and if so should it use inline config hot reload or a lifecycle-loaded file path rather than per-event file reads?
rationale: The choice establishes long-lived configuration, precedence, reload, and operator-failure semantics that cannot be safely inferred from implementation details alone.

options.title: Use inline hot-reloaded config
options.body: Keep a single inline Home view setting and rely on canonical OpenClaw config hot reload, avoiding a second path contract and event-time filesystem access.

options.title: Load files at lifecycle boundaries
options.body: Retain `viewPath`, but resolve and validate it during account activation or explicit config reload rather than for every Slack event.

options.title: Keep the built-in view only
options.body: Decline the new configuration surface and retain the existing safe App Home behavior until a stronger operator workflow is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Use inline hot-reloaded config
recommendation.body: Keep a single inline Home view setting and rely on canonical OpenClaw config hot reload, avoiding a second path contract and event-time filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: The current App Home behavior appears to originate from their merged implementation, making them the strongest history-backed owner for the permanent contract.
